Intitulée la “marche des paniers vides”, cette mobilisation avait pour but d’accentuer la pression sur le gouvernement afin d’obtenir des mesures concrètes.

france24fr.title: Allemagne : ouverture des bureaux de vote en Saxe-Anhalt, où l'AfD vise une victoire historique
france24fr.description: Les bureaux de vote ont ouvert, dimanche matin, en Saxe-Anhalt, dans l'est de l'Allemagne, où l'extrême droite est en passe de remporter les élections régionales et vise la direction de cet État régional d'ex-RDA. Une percée inédite dans l'Allemagne depuis 1945, qui fragiliserait davantage le chancelier Friedrich Merz.

france24fr.title: En direct : après Moscou, les émissaires de Trump se rendent pour la première fois en Ukraine
france24fr.description: Les émissaires américains Steve Witkoff et Jared Kushner se rendent, dimanche, en Ukraine pour la première fois, porteurs, selon le président Donald Trump, d'une proposition destinée à mettre fin au conflit avec la Russie. La veille, ils ont rencontré Vladimir Poutine à Moscou. Suivez notre direct.

france24fr.title: Mutinerie au Niger : les autorités accusent à nouveau la France et "ses valets africains"
france24fr.description: Près d’une semaine après la mutinerie qui a secoué le Niger,le porte-parole du gouvernement a lu publiquement un court message et accuse la France et ses « valets africains » d’être responsables de la tentative de coup d’État du 29 août dernier. Un discours habituel depuis la prise de pouvoir des militaires au Niger en 2023 mais qui cette fois ne cite pas nommément les pays précédemment accusés, comme le Tchad.

france24fr.title: Mercato : pourquoi les joueurs africains valent-ils désormais plus de 100 millions d’euros ?
france24fr.description:
Les joueurs africains affolent les compteurs du mercato mondial. L’Ivoirien Yan Diomandé est devenu le joueur africain le plus cher de l’histoire avec son transfert au Real Madrid pour 125 millions d’euros hors bonus. Le Marocain Ayyoub Bouaddi a lui rejoint Manchester City dans une opération pouvant atteindre 100 millions d’euros.

Des montants records pour des joueurs très jeunes, dans un marché également dopé par la Coupe du monde 2026.

france24fr.title: Lyes Louffok: "le projet de loi sur la protection des enfants n'est absolument pas à la hauteur"
france24fr.description: Plus de 3 mois après la découverte du corps de la jeune Lyhanna, le rapport définitif sur les dysfonctionnements qui ont pu mener à ce drame est attendu en pleine rentrée politique, à 7 mois et demi de la présidentielle, et 2 jours avant l'arrivée en commission à l'Assemblée de la proposition de loi intégrale contre les violences sexistes et sexuelles. Lyes Louffok, ancien enfant placé, militant pour les droits des enfants en France, était l'invité d'Au Cœur de l'Info.

france24fr.title: Allemagne : 6 000 personnes manifestent pour la démocratie avant un scrutin favorable à l'AfD
france24fr.description: Près de 6 000 personnes ont manifesté samedi à Magdebourg, dans la région de Saxe-Anhalt, en Allemagne. Le rassemblement était organisé dans le cadre d'un festival pour "la démocratie" à la veille d'un scrutin régional qui pourrait être remporté par l'extrême droite.

france24fr.title: Cessez-le-feu temporaire à Kiev pendant trois jours alors que les émissaires américains s'y rendent
france24fr.description: Le président russe Vladimir Poutine a ordonné, samedi, de cesser les frappes sur Kiev pendant trois jours, alors que les Américains Steve Witkoff et Jared Kushner doivent s'y rendre. Les deux émissaires du président américain ont atterri à Moscou avec un plan visant à mettre fin à plus de quatre ans de guerre en Ukraine.

france24fr.title: Moyen-Orient : l'Iran annonce des représailles après des frappes américaines sur des pétroliers
france24fr.description: Téhéran a annoncé samedi avoir mené des représailles sur "trois pétroliers" dans le détroit d'Ormuz ainsi que trois autres navires "affiliés à l'Amérique", après que l'armée américaine ait détruit plus tôt trois pétroliers iraniens de le golfe Arabo-Persique.

france24fr.title: Élections en Israël : un superflic juif candidat sur une liste arabe, une "révolution"
france24fr.description: Yoav Segalovitz, un ancien policier et ministre juif, sera numéro deux sur la liste du parti arabe israélien Ra'am aux élections du 27 octobre 2026. Cette annonce faite le 31 août détonne dans un climat électoral où l'extrême droite stigmatise toujours plus les Palestiniens citoyens d'Israël. Elle pourrait cependant ouvrir la voie à l'inclusion d'un parti arabe dans une coalition d'opposition à Netanyahu et ses alliés.

france24fr.title: Visite des émissaires américains : Poutine ordonne l'arrêt des frappes sur Kiev pendant trois jours
france24fr.description: Le président russe Vladimir Poutine a ordonné, samedi, de cesser les frappes sur Kiev pendant trois jours, alors que les Américains Steve Witkoff et Jared Kushner doivent s'y rendre. Les deux émissaires du président américain ont atterri à Moscou avec un plan visant à mettre fin à plus de quatre ans de guerre en Ukraine.

france24fr.title: Plus de 5 000 disparus au Népal : des crémations symboliques à Katmandou
france24fr.description: Au Népal, le dernier bilan de la crue meurtrière après l’effondrement d’une partie d’un glacier est de 1 287 morts et 5 083 disparus selon l’autorité népalaise chargée de la gestion des situations d’urgence. De nombreuses familles tentent de faire le deuil de leurs proches, malgré parfois l’absence de corps. Notre envoyée spéciale au Népal, Ondine de Gaulle, s’est rendue sur le site de crémation Pashupati Aryaghat à Katmandou.

france24fr.title: L'ancienne ministre Rachida Dati de retour dans la magistrature avant son procès pour corruption
france24fr.description: Ancienne ministre de la Justice et de la Culture, Rachida Dati, a annoncé vouloir réintégrer la magistrature. Une annonce qui a fait réagir, alors qu'elle sera jugée du 16 au 28 septembre pour corruption. Une source judiciaire a affirmé, samedi, qu'elle ne pourra cependant pas exercer en juridiction, c'est-à-dire ni dans un tribunal ni dans une cour.

france24fr.title: Au Népal, que sait-on des deux rescapés de la catastrophe samedi ?
france24fr.description: Les secours népalais sont parvenus samedi à extraire une personne, de nationalité chinoise, d'un tunnel du nord du pays où il était retenu prisonnier depuis la coulée de boue meurtrière du 26 août, après qu'un pan d'un glacier ce soit effondré. Par ailleurs, les services du Premier ministre népalais ont annoncé samedi le sauvetage d'une femme de 64 ans, Chandrika Shrestha, retrouvée vivante dans une maison de la localité sinistrée de Betrawati.

france24fr.title: Amnesty international alerte sur la détention en Arabie saoudite du franco-égyptien Amr Abdelfattah
france24fr.description: Ingénieur-chercheur franco-égyptien en télécommunications, Amr Abdelfattah est détenu en Arabie saoudite depuis juin 2024, après avoir été arrêté lors d’un pèlerinage à La Mecque. Présenté à la justice saoudienne en mai 2025, il a finalement été condamné à huit ans de prison, notamment pour avoir prétendument insulté le gouvernement saoudien. Amnesty International plaide pour sa libération. Les précisions avec Julia Basile, avocate d’Amr Abdelfattah, invitée de France 24.

spiegel.description: Als Hans Noltes Frau stirbt, weiß er nicht mehr weiter. Dann meldet er sich für die Tischtennis-WM der Senioren an – und findet in Südkorea, wonach er lange gesucht hat.

spiegel.title: Rätsel der Woche: Auf welche zwei Ziffern endet 7 hoch 9999?
spiegel.description: Die dritte Potenz von 7 ist 343. Diese Zahl endet auf 43. Wissen Sie auch, welche zwei Ziffern bei der deutlich größeren Potenz 7 hoch 9999 am Schluss stehen?

spiegel.title: Israel baut Barriere im Jordantal: Krieg gegen die Felder, die Bäume und die Menschen
spiegel.description: Israelische Soldaten errichten nahe der Grenze zu Jordanien eine Barriere, die palästinensische Bauern von ihrem Land abschneidet. Vor Ort wird klar: Der Wall soll offenbar auch dazu dienen, das Jordantal komplett zu besiedeln.

spiegel.title: Berlin-Hack: Grünenpolitiker Konstantin von Notz sieht Leaks als »echten Daten-Super-GAU«
spiegel.description: Hacker haben die Berliner Verwaltung angegriffen, erpresst und mit Datenleaks bloßgestellt. Der Grünenfraktionsvize Konstantin von Notz macht dem Land Berlin und der Bundesregierung Vorwürfe.

spiegel.title: News: Warum wir bei Russland an Sting denken sollten – die Lage am Sonntag
spiegel.description: Deutschland hat einen Feind. Nun hilft vor allem Besonnenheit. Und ein Lied. Das ist die Lage am Sonntag.

spiegel.title: Schöner schreiben: Hildegard Hamm-Brücher und die Kraft der rhetorischen Ohrfeige
spiegel.description: Unser Kolumnist zeigt an Beispielen aus der Literatur, wie kraftvoll die deutsche Sprache sein kann. Folge 137: Hildegard Hamm-Brücher wirbt für Anstand in der Politik.

spiegel.title: Krieg in der Ukraine: Kreml lobt Friedensgespräche mit US-Unterhändlern
spiegel.description: Jared Kushner, der Schwiegersohn von US-Präsident Trump, und Steve Witkoff haben mit Wladimir Putin gesprochen, diesen Sonntag treffen sie Wolodymyr Selenskyj. Die russische Seite zeigt sich angetan.

spiegel.title: Sachsen-Anhalt live – News zur Landtagswahl: Die Wahllokale in Sachsen-Anhalt sind geöffnet
spiegel.description: Rund 1,7 Millionen Wahlberechtigte können in Sachsen-Anhalt ihre Stimme abgeben. Die Wahlurnen stehen bereit. Und: Magdeburger Bischof predigt gegen die AfD. Die Entwicklungen im Newsblog.

spiegel.title: Bundesliga: Aufsteiger Schalke gegen FC Bayern: Sie rannten bis das Arenadach wegflog
spiegel.description: Schalke ringt Rekordmeister Bayern ein Unentschieden ab. Der Aufsteiger schafft das auch dank einer Motivationsspritze von Eminem. Und dann hatte Manuel Neuer noch eine besondere Sichtweise auf die Pfiffe gegen ihn.

spiegel.title: Klosterbrauerei: Schwester Doris verwandelt Wasser zu Bier – die guten News der Woche
spiegel.description: Eine Nonne aus Bayern verwandelt Wasser in Bier. Eine Philippinerin löst die »Eala-Mania« aus. Und: So kommen Sie nach dem Urlaub wieder entspannt in die Arbeit. Das sind die guten Nachrichten der Woche.

spiegel.title: Unterwäsche: Einmal im Leben so bequeme Unterhosen tragen wie ein Mann
spiegel.description: Ich habe mich zu lange mit spitzenbesäumten Slips aus Polyester herumgeschlagen. Und eine Entscheidung getroffen, die weit über das Private hinausgeht.

spiegel.title: Sachsen-Anhalt: Was Sie über die Landtagswahl wissen sollten
spiegel.description: Regieren bald Rechtsextreme ein Bundesland? Kommt es zur Koalition zwischen CDU und Linken? Und warum fällt eine womöglich entscheidende Rolle den Grünen zu? Fragen und Antworten zur Sachsen-Anhalt-Wahl.

spiegel.title: Deutschland: Wie lässt sich die Spaltung zwischen Ost und West überwinden?
spiegel.description: Deutschland wird immer ostdeutscher, sagt der Soziologe Armin Nassehi. Der Osten wird vom Westen herabgesetzt, erwidert der Germanist Dirk Oschmann. Der SPIEGEL hat beide zusammengebracht. Hier suchen sie nach Lösungen.

spiegel.title: Landtagswahl Sachsen-Anhalt: Monika Schnitzer warnt vor Risiken bei AfD-Regierung
spiegel.description: Sachsen-Anhalt wählt heute einen neuen Landtag. Die AfD liegt in Umfragen vorn. Die Chefin der Wirtschaftsweisen, Monika Schnitzer, warnt: Eine AfD-Regierung könnte dringend benötigte Fachkräfte und Unternehmen vergraulen.

spiegel.title: Kritische Infrastruktur: Cem Özdemir fordert Hochdruckprogramm zum besseren Schutz
spiegel.description: Anschläge auf Umspannwerke, Sprengstoffvorrichtungen, ein Drohnenangriff: Deutschlands kritische Infrastruktur steht unter Beschuss. Baden-Württembergs Ministerpräsident Özdemir verlangt nun bundesweite Konsequenzen.

spiegel.title: Sozialstaat: Verbände warnen vor Einschnitten bei Wohngeld, Elterngeld, Rente
spiegel.description: Sozialkürzungen beim Wohngeld, beim Elterngeld, bei der Rente: Zum Start der Haushaltsberatungen schlagen Gewerkschaften und Wohlfahrtsverbände Alarm. Sie fordern, den Sozialstaat nicht dem Verteidigungshaushalt zu opfern.

observador.title: Arouca Film Festival com 40 obras a concurso
observador.description: "É uma mostra ampla de filmes vindo de todo o mundo, feira por realizadores conceituados e jovens promessas", afirma o diretor do festival, João Rita.

observador.title: Após Moscovo, enviados norte-americanos chegam hoje a Kiev
observador.description: Enviados dos EUA, Jared Kushner e Steve Witkoff, chegam este domingo a Kiev após reunião com Putin em Moscovo. Rússia parou ataques a Kiev por 72 horas, mas continua a atacar outros pontos da Ucrânia.

observador.title: Ilha do Fogo: 22 mortos em acidente de autocarro escolar
observador.description: De acordo com as autoridades, o "autocarro transportava alunos num passeio" quando saiu da estrada e caiu de uma altura de cerca de 30 metros, em Campanas de Cima, município de Santa Catarina do Fogo.

observador.title: 9h. Kremlin diz que conversações em Moscovo são positivas
observador.description: Conselheiro do presidente russo considerou as negociações “oportunas e muito benéficas para ambos os lados”. Ainda, no desporto, Sporting e Benfica vencem as partidas referentes à quinta jornada.

observador.title: "Succederà questa notte": Nanni Moretti corre pelo Leão
observador.description: É a história de uma paixão persistente, um filme obstinado e romanesco, com Louis Garrel e Jasmine Trinca. Dividiu o Lido  — mas não foi Moretti sempre assim?

observador.title: 8h. Sete distritos sob aviso amarelo devido ao tempo quente
observador.description: É o que avisa o Instituto Português do Mar e da Atmosfera. Ainda, Chega defende que a moção de censura vai "separar o trigo do joio".

observador.title: Em Espanha, a VW “mata” a Seat. E a Autoeuropa tem futuro?
observador.description: Depois dos 100.000 despedimentos e das quatro fábricas encerradas, o Grupo VW avança para o encerramento de marcas, com a Seat a ser a primeira vítima. E qual será o futuro da portuguesa Autoeuropa?

observador.title: "Furei os rótulos quando só queriam manequins esqueléticas"
observador.description: Fátima Lopes sempre marcou a moda pela independência. A criadora reflete sobre o seu percurso, a defesa da igualdade e da inclusão, a recusa em perdoar traições e o papel da autoestima de uma mulher.

observador.title: 7h. Quase 300 operacionais combatem chamas em Estremoz
observador.description: Proteção Civil do Alentejo Central revela que chamas estão a ceder, mas o incêndio ainda não está controlado. Ainda, PS volta a acusar o Governo de lucrar com o aumento dos preços dos combustíveis.

observador.title: 6h. Extrema-direita pode conquistar primeiro estado alemão
observador.description: AfD (Alternativa para a Alemanha) lidera as sondagens e pode conseguir resultado histórico. Ainda, cerca de 400 operacionais combatem dois incêndios ativos no país em Évora e em Portalegre.

observador.title: Sabia que a Língua Gestual Portuguesa tem sotaques?
observador.description: Marco Neves desmistifica mitos sobre a Língua Gestual Portuguesa, analisa os diferentes nomes dados ao pão pelo país e revela porque é que "arigato" não vem de "obrigado" nem "azulejo" de "azul".

observador.title: O preço das casas já passou o patamar do absurdo? — Ouvintes
observador.description: Susana Peralta responde sobre se é possível esperar um recuo no mercado imobiliário e também sobre onde andará o Pacto Estratégico de Seguro para a Saúde — e se devíamos estar a ouvir mais sobre ele.

observador.title: 5h. Enviados dos EUA reúnem-se com Zelensky em Kiev
observador.description: Depois de Moscovo, Witkoff e Kushner visitam a capital ucraniana para relançar negociações de paz entre Rússia e Ucrânia. Ainda, sete distritos sob aviso amarelo devido ao calor até segunda.

observador.title: 4h. Combustíveis. Soares diz que Carneiro vive no passado
observador.description: Secretário-geral do PSD acusa líder socialista de ter ficado preso aos tempos do PS no Governo. Ainda, fenómeno de vento e granizo atinge Albergaria-a-Velha e deixa rasto de destruição.

observador.title: 3h. PS volta a acusar Governo de lucrar com combustíveis
observador.description: Eurico Brilhante Dias diz que, desde 2024, Governo já encaixou mais de mil milhões de euros em receitas provenientes dos aumentos. Ainda, André Ventura diz moção de censura vai separar trigo do joio.

observador.title: 2h. PCP diz que Governo se deixou arrastar pelo MAI
observador.description: Paulo Raimundo considera que Luís Neves tem muitas explicações a dar, mas, para já, não revela o sentido de voto do partido. Ainda, Sporting vence Nacional por 2-0 e Benfica bate Marítimo por 3-0.

observador.title: 1h. Albergaria-a-Velha. Vento e granizo provocam estragos
observador.description: Coordenador municipal da Proteção Civil dá conta de casas e veículos danificados. Ainda nesta edição, Eurico Brilhante Dias responde a Hugo Soares sobre preços dos combustíveis.

observador.title: Meloni e a Itália
observador.description: Em grande medida, o feito de Meloni é este: o sistema político conseguiu finalmente colocar na chefia do governo um líder partidário escolhido por uma maioria do povo, à frente de uma coligação

elpais.title: Marruecos, envalentonado: Mohamed VI se crece gracias al apoyo de Trump (y de Israel)
elpais.description: La crisis de Ceuta ha dejado bien clara una cosa: Rabat ha actuado con la tranquilidad que da saberse respaldado por Estados Unidos. En 2020 Donald Trump reconoció la soberanía marroquí sobre el Sáhara Occidental, lo que ha dado alas al país norteafricano para expandir su política exterior y reactivar la cuestión de la soberanía sobre Ceuta y Melilla

elpais.title: Última hora de la entrada de inmigrantes a Ceuta, en directo | Trump ve “triste” lo que pasa en Ceuta y dice que España no controla su frontera
elpais.description: El presidente de EE UU vuelve a aludir al caso de la ciudad autónoma en un mensaje publicado en Truth | Vivas se reunirá el martes en Bruselas con comisarios de la UE

elpais.title: Ceuta, atrapada en la guerra política
elpais.description: El boicoteo de la ciudad a varios espacios, evidenciado por la guerra en el puerto, ha alargado la crisis. El Gobierno desclasifica este martes los documentos para probar que nadie vio venir un salto tan grande

elpais.title: Las otras crisis de Interior que marcan el paso a Marlaska en Ceuta
elpais.description: El ministro cuenta con precedentes como el cese de Pérez de los Cobos, la imputación de la directora de la Guardia Civil o la condena por las devoluciones en caliente en 2021 que, inevitablemente, encorsetan su gestión

elpais.title: La vuelta al cole en Ceuta: “De material escolar, lo primero es el gas pimienta”
elpais.description: Los centros de primaria de la ciudad autónoma regresan a las clases esta semana con seguridad privada y mayor presencia policial en las calles

elpais.title: Escalada de amenazas en las fronteras de Europa
elpais.description: La más que probable intensificación del conflicto bélico en Ucrania en otoño se suma a la guerra híbrida que ha emprendido Rusia contra la Unión Europea

elpais.title: Tomoko Akane, presidenta del Tribunal Penal Internacional: “Tarde o temprano la Historia nos pedirá cuentas a todos. ¿Dónde estabas?"
elpais.description: Sancionada por Estados Unidos, la magistrada considera que el TPI afronta la mayor crisis desde su creación pero cree que la búsqueda de justicia es una responsabilidad compartida y un derecho de las víctimas

elpais.title: Wittenoom: españoles en el ‘Chernóbil’ australiano
elpais.description: Dos familias de emigrantes de los sesenta relatan el drama de la mina de amianto que ha causado más de 2.000 muertes

elpais.title: Lindsay Clancy y el monstruo de Frankenstein
elpais.description: Mary Shelley ya diagnosticó ese doble rasero por el cual al varón lo dotamos de un dolor trágico que a una mujer siempre le negaríamos

elpais.title: Lo aguantamos (casi) todo
elpais.description: Hablo de la porfía misma del cuerpo y de un montón de amenazas invisibles con las que convivimos

elpais.title: ¿Tiene usted miedo?
elpais.description: Echo en falta ante las preocupaciones por la IA ideas sobre qué podemos hacer los civiles sin poder en una sociedad tan poco organizada

elpais.title: Hoy no cerramos
elpais.description: La velocidad es consustancial al periodismo, pero la calidad exige tiempo, revisión y edición, mucha edición

elpais.title: Leonormanía, ¿mito o realidad?: “Leonor interesa cuando se acerca a los mortales”
elpais.description: La princesa de Asturias empieza la universidad este lunes. Ahora, más jóvenes quieren estudiar Ciencias Políticas como ella en la Carlos III de Madrid, pero, ¿hasta dónde llega la influencia de la heredera sobre los españoles? Opinan politólogos, expertos en realeza e ‘influencers’

elpais.title: Cómo Rodri se ganó al Camp Nou: el miedo de Pedri y la ansiedad de una hinchada que ya corea su canción
elpais.description: El capitán de la selección española conquista al cuerpo técnico y busca liderar el vestuario ahora que tiene rendida a la afición azulgrana

elpais.title: Alicia Giménez Bartlett: “Ahora a las viejas nos pelotean porque tenemos la pasta”
elpais.description: La escritora, de 75 años, publica ‘Bajo el cielo infernal’,  nuevo caso de la saga de la inspectora Petra Delicado, personaje que creó hace 30 años. Ambas, autora y personaje, han enviudado y pasan el duelo cada una a su manera

elpais.title: Se busca fiesta clandestina en villa de Ibiza
elpais.description: Los ‘afters’ ilegales de la isla se mueven en Telegram y se ocultan en sótanos de fincas para evitar crecientes multas y desalojos

elpais.title: Viajar fuera de temporada alta: los precios, la masificación y el clima cambian el turismo
elpais.description: Los turistas empiezan a contratar sus vacaciones en otros meses distintos a los tradicionales, y optan mayoritariamente por mayo, septiembre o octubre

elpais.title: Segregar a los extranjeros y relativizar el nazismo: así se acerca la extrema derecha al poder en Alemania
elpais.description: Una victoria del partido AfD este domingo en la región de Sajonia-Anhalt representa un peligro para el Estado de derecho y para Europa, afirman las instituciones del Estado

nyt.title: Trump Officials Draft Plan to Pay At-Home Parents, Using Funds for Working Ones
nyt.description: The proposed benefit, a top policy priority for Vice President JD Vance, would apply only to married couples and tap a fund intended to provide federal child care subsidies to working parents.

nyt.title: Inside the D.O.J.’s Investigation of Fauci and Other Virus Scientists
nyt.description: As Dr. Anthony Fauci has faced public scrutiny from congressional Republicans, the D.O.J. has pursued a quieter and more expansive effort against a wider circle of researchers.

nyt.title: Putin Meets Witkoff and Kushner in Moscow to Discuss Ukraine War
nyt.description: President Vladimir V. Putin ordered a pause in strikes on Ukraine’s capital, Kyiv, ahead of the meeting with President Trump’s envoys: his son-in-law Jared Kushner and the businessman Steve Witkoff.

nyt.title: U.S. Strikes Three Iranian ‘Shadow Network’ Oil Tankers, Military Says
nyt.description: The U.S. military said it retaliated after Iran launched missiles at two warships. The strikes came days after the two sides exchanged some of their most intense fire in weeks.

nyt.title: What the War in Iran Has Cost One Gold Star Family
nyt.description: First Lt. Tyler James Feehan, who was 25, had been deployed to an air base in Jordan when enemy missiles and drones lit up the sky. He is among the 18 Americans who have died since the war began.

nyt.title: A Sympathetic Defendant and Well-Crafted Defense Dominated Clancy Trial
nyt.description: The defense lawyer for Lindsay Clancy showed empathy for his client in showcasing her mental health problems. That may have made all the difference.

nyt.title: What Will Happen to Lindsay Clancy in the Long Term?
nyt.description: Even as a jury failed to reach a verdict in Lindsay Clancy’s murder trial, her future is unlikely to include freedom, at least for a long time. But Americans have been divided over the goal of her confinement.

nyt.title: Will Lindsay Clancy Be Retried? The Decision Now Facing Prosecutor Timothy Cruz.
nyt.description: After a mistrial, Timothy Cruz must decide whether to retry Lindsay Clancy on first-degree murder charges, downgrade the charges or drop the case.

nyt.title: In Germany, Ulrich Siegmund Is Bringing the AfD to the Cusp of Power
nyt.description: Ulrich Siegmund, 35, once sold air fresheners. Now his far-right party is the favorite to win a state election in eastern Germany on Sunday.

nyt.title: Elections in Germany Could Produce First Far-Right State Government Since Nazi Era: What to Know
nyt.description: Elections in Saxony-Anhalt, in the country’s east, could result in an outright majority for the Alternative for Germany party.

nyt.title: Nepal Floods Buried a House. The Woman Inside Was Still Alive.
nyt.description: A rescue from a mostly buried house gave new hope to a town devastated by floods in Nepal. Earlier Saturday, another survivor had been pulled from a tunnel.

nyt.title: Harlan Coben’s New Book Is a Tough-Talking Writing Guide
nyt.description: Even a very successful thriller writer fights self-doubt. His new tough-talking writing guide doubles as a memoir that explains why, and how to beat it.

nyt.title: It’s Not Just the West Bank Settlers. It’s Israel.
nyt.description: Settler violence is reaching new heights.

nyt.title: A New World Order Is Coming. We Aren’t Ready.
nyt.description: We must be honest about the seriousness of the situation we’re in.

nyt.title: China’s New Graduates, Facing a Dire Job Market, Must Also Contend With A.I.
nyt.description: A record 12.7 million young people are looking for jobs as the country embraces artificial intelligence — and as the technology begins to upend the work force.

npr.title: U.S. strikes three Iranian oil tankers in renewal of hostilities
npr.description: The U.S. strikes three Iranian oil tankers after Iran targets two American warships, in the latest exchange over shipping and the Strait of Hormuz.

npr.title: This is the work of our lifetime: Ayana Elizabeth Johnson urges action after new UN climate report
npr.description: A United Nations report has found that the world will warm to 1.5 degrees Celsius above pre-industrial levels. Climate solutions advocate Ayana Elizabeth Johnson urges a quicker implementation of known strategies - and determination rather than despair.

npr.title: U.S. strikes Iranian oil tankers in retaliation for missile attacks on Navy ships
npr.description: One of the Iranian tankers struck was near a key area in Iran's oil-export system, according to U.S. Central Command.

npr.title: How the U.S. focus on Iran is fueling a more aggressive Putin
npr.description: Trump's top envoys head to Moscow and Kyiv as Putin steps up round the clock bombing of Ukraine. With the U.S. distracted by Iran, is Putin becoming increasingly emboldened?

npr.title: U.S.-Venezuela oil deal puts opposition in a political bind
npr.description: Venezuelan opposition members are uneasy with new oil deals with the U.S., worried that agreements with authoritarian regime in Caracas could undermine democratic progress.

npr.title: U.S. envoys in Moscow in new push for peace between Russia and Ukraine
npr.description: U.S. envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner have arrived in Moscow to revive efforts to end Russia's invasion of Ukraine. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has called for a halt to air attacks during their visit, but Moscow has not publicly responded.

npr.title: Philippines Vice President Sara Duterte posts bail after arrest
npr.description: Philippines Vice President Sara Duterte has posted bail after order issued for her arrest on charges she publicly threatened to arrange assassination of President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. and two others.

npr.title: The U.N. backs a new world map showing Africa in its true relative size
npr.description: The U.N. has backed a new map showing Africa in its true relative size, with the U.S. standing alone in opposition.

npr.title: Philippine vice president is ordered arrested for threats against the president
npr.description: It's part of a political showdown with Marcos. A trial could impact her plans to run for president in 2028.

npr.title: Myanmar military head visits Vietnam to normalize relations
npr.description: His trip to Vietnam marks his third visit to an ASEAN member state as he seeks to restore Myanmar's standing in the bloc.

republika.description: Due vittorie nelle prime due partite per il club del Saarland, che domenica prossima affronterà in casa proprio la corazzata bavarese

Dal dramma dei genitori

republika.description: L’analista politico Anton Barbashin: “Il presidente americano resta l’unico mediatore possibile, la Ue è considerata parte del conflitto”

republika.description: Al Forum Ambrosetti va in scena la sfida tra l’ex premier e il fondatore di Futuro nazionale. L’eurodeputato rivendica il suo no all’incremento della spesa militare: “La Russia non attaccherà il continente”. Il senatore a vita: “In lei la ricostruzione dello spirito del Ventennio”

republika.description: Mazzoncini (A2a): “il generale poco concreto”. L’ex ministro Padoan: “Bello quello che ha detto l’ex premier. Tutti dovrebbero sentirlo”

republika.description: Le cinque proposte Pd per affrontare le crisi su energia e clima:“Sono la stessa battaglia”

republika.description: La segretaria di Noi Moderati: “Pulsioni antidemocratiche” dall’ex militare. Al Forum Ambrosetti “cedimento dell’establishment”

republika.description: Il leader del Rassemblement national: “Vogliamo rendere la Francia uno dei paesi meno attrattivi per l’immigrazione

republika.description: L’influencer Hannes Kreschel: “A sedici anni io votavo Afd, oggi vi spiego perché sono pericolosi. Le idee hitleriane non si sono mai estinte del tutto”

phys-org.title: Germany's Isar Aerospace launches rocket into orbit from Norway
phys-org.description: Germany's Isar Aerospace launched a rocket into orbit from Norway on Saturday as Europe races to boost its ability to economically send satellites into space independently of the United States.

phys-org.title: Haze emergency grips Malaysian Borneo town
phys-org.description: Acrid smoke hung heavily over the Malaysian town of Serian, seeping into homes and cloaking roadside stalls, as residents navigated an air-quality emergency fueled by transboundary haze from Indonesia's raging fires.

phys-org.title: Breaking through AlphaFold's limits to predict how proteins change shape
phys-org.description: Conformational changes in proteins are vital to their function yet remain challenging for state-of-the-art artificial intelligence, such as AlphaFold3, to predict. Researchers at the Institute for Molecular Science (IMS), and the Graduate University for Advanced Studies, SOKENDAI introduced a repulsive force between predicted structures, allowing AlphaFold3 to sample the multiple conformational states that its default settings rarely capture.

phys-org.title: How much clearcutting can nature sustain? A study determines the ecological limit for boreal forest birds
phys-org.description: A study led by the University of Jyväskylä in Finland evaluated, for the first time, an ecological threshold for the amount of clearcutting in boreal forests. According to the results, maintaining populations of bird species specialized in old-growth forests requires either a forest rotation period of at least 90 years on average or that approximately one-fifth of the forest area be excluded from clearcut management. The study provides a concrete target for the ecologically sustainable use of fo

phys-org.title: FAST finds two mysterious hydrogen clouds with no visible stars
phys-org.description: Astronomers have found two clouds of hydrogen near the Whirlpool galaxy that appear to contain almost no stars. The clouds, discovered with China's FAST radio telescope, each contain roughly 3 million times the mass of the sun in hydrogen but have no detectable optical counterpart. Their properties are outlined in a new paper published in the Astronomy & Astrophysics  journal on Aug. 4.

phys-org.title: Views from a physician and veterinarian: How to improve barriers to pet care when owners are hospitalized
phys-org.description: The human-animal bond is often so strong that pet owners may delay or forgo medical treatment or leave a health care facility against medical advice if they have no one to care for their pet at home. A perspective paper published in the New England Journal of Medicine explains why pet owners may need different approaches to care when hospitalized, according to an Emory University physician and an Ohio State University veterinarian.

phys-org.title: US study tests psilocybin to fight cancer side effects
phys-org.description: Here's a novel idea for countering the painful side effects of chemotherapy: Beforehand, take the hallucinogenic drug found in magic mushrooms.

phys-org.title: A black hole as light as 40 tons can exist inside a star if dark matter helps
phys-org.description: In 1974, Stephen Hawking made a prediction that transformed our understanding of black holes. Black holes, he showed, are not truly black: They slowly lose energy through a quantum process now known as Hawking radiation. The lighter the black hole, the faster it evaporates.

phys-org.title: Tree species diversity protects forests from climate extremes, study finds
phys-org.description: New research has found that tree species diversity can play a crucial role in protecting forests from the growing threat of extreme climate events. The study analyzed data from 88,116 separate forest plots across the United States to investigate the impact of "compound climate extremes," when events such as drought and extreme heat occur at the same time.

phys-org.title: Scientists discover how narwhals grow nature's only straight tusk
phys-org.description: Narwhals have nature's only straight tusk, a single tooth up to three meters (10 feet) long, so strange they were sold as magical unicorn horns during the Middle Ages.

phys-org.title: Some disagreement makes groups more trustworthy, mathematical framework finds
phys-org.description: When humans are making decisions, they are known not to rely solely on their own considerations and the evidence available to them. Past behavioral science and psychology studies have shown that people are often also influenced by the choices and opinions of others.

phys-org.title: Lakes aren't just storing water—they're changing the carbon cycle
phys-org.description: Lakes may look like picturesque stopping points along a river or stream, but they can have a big influence on what happens to carbon as it moves through a landscape. New research suggests that the more lake-rich a network of streams is, the more carbon is released into the atmosphere rather than carried downstream.

phys-org.title: Ocean indicators NOAA scientists are tracking for El Niño's arrival on the West Coast
phys-org.description: Has El Niño reached the West Coast? You might think it has. After all, the ocean off Southern and Central California is unusually warm. But that warmth is from a recent marine heat wave that predates the current El Niño. Much of the Pacific Coast is experiencing relatively normal conditions while still awaiting the impacts of what could be a very strong El Niño.

phys-org.title: Late Roman decrees uncover military system behind amphitheater animal spectacles
phys-org.description: A study on Roman law by the Carlos III University of Madrid analyzes the regulations and complex imperial logistics governing the capture, transport and safety of animals used in spectacles in the Roman Empire—which were far more popular than gladiatorial combat.

phys-org.title: New method predicts where massive earthquakes will strike
phys-org.description: UC Riverside scientists have developed a way to identify where Earth's biggest earthquakes are most likely to occur, offering a powerful new tool for improving disaster preparation in some of the most dangerous seismic regions.

phys-org.title: How haze from Indonesian fires impacts Southeast Asia
phys-org.description: Thick smog has blanketed parts of Indonesia as the vast archipelago battles fires that have burned large swaths of Borneo and Sumatra for weeks.

phys-org.title: Indonesia rescues second orangutan mother and baby from wildfire
phys-org.description: An orangutan mother and her baby, threatened by wildfires encroaching on their habitat in Indonesia, were rescued earlier this week, authorities said in a statement Saturday.

phys-org.title: Spacecraft bound for Mercury begins 'tricky' arrival
phys-org.description: After an eight-year journey, a spacecraft carrying European and Japanese probes began the monthslong, high-risk approach to Mercury on Thursday to study the sun-scorched planet.

undark.title: Book Review: The Messy Business of Making Science Happen
undark.description: In “Lost in Curiosity: Field Notes From Scientists’ Adventures Into the Unknown,” Roberta Kwok sets out to smash the stereotype of eureka moments as the main drivers of scientific knowledge, largely by taking us inside the everyday world of science and scientists, in all its painstaking monotony.

undark.title: Book Review: Our Conflicted Relationship with the Sun
undark.description: Despite dermatological guidelines that decree sunlight a harmful carcinogen, Rowan Jacobsen argues in “In Defense of Sunlight” that the sun helps our skin produce many compounds vital to our health. How did science miss these benefits? The answer, he says, lies in our inability to do things in moderation.

undark.title: The New Student Visa Policy Doesn’t Add Up
undark.description: In July, the Department of Homeland Security issued new rules that would make it harder for international students to complete their studies in the U.S. The policy threatens to be disruptive for students — particularly doctoral candidates — and self-defeating for the country.

undark.title: Book Review: How Wildlife Is Returning to the East
undark.description: In “The Beasts of the East,” journalist Andrew Moore charts the natural history of the East and the people who have dedicated their careers to restoring several long lost species to what remains of their original habitats.

undark.title: Book Review: The Case for the AI-Powered Global Brain
undark.description: In “The God Test,” Robert Wright considers a future in which human consciousness becomes infused with AI. “We have to think seriously about a future in which there is something that increasingly resembles a global brain, and its neurons increasingly consist not just of human brains but of AIs,” he writes.

undark.title: Interview: How Tragedy Changed the FDA
undark.description: As an FDA advisory committee prepares to weigh whether specialized pharmacies should be allowed to dispense seven unapproved peptides, Mikkael A. Sekeres, a scientist and former adviser, discusses the history and nuances of FDA oversight, including its process for screening advisory committee members for conflicts of interest.

undark.title: Will AI Fix Prior Authorization — or Make It Worse?
undark.description: The Trump administration is currently piloting a program in six states that expands Medicare prior authorizations using AI tools in an effort to reduce unnecessary medical spending. But it remains to be seen whether this new approach, which the administration has called “broken” in the private sector, will be effective without causing dangerous delays for Medicare recipients.

undark.title: Biologists Should Articulate Their Position on AI
undark.description: Last month, mathematics researchers released the Leiden Declaration, a treatise on how to handle the challenges that artificial intelligence poses to their field. C. Brandon Ogbunu argues that biologists should learn from the mathematics community and work on their own version.

undark.title: Review: What Animals Can Teach Humans About Caregiving
undark.description: From seahorses and birds to beetles and killer whales, journalist Elizabeth Preston finds a lot of common ground  between human and animal parenting in “The Creatures’ Guide to Caring,” a sweeping survey of the evolution of caregiving and the dizzying array of survival strategies in the animal kingdom.

undark.title: The MAHA Movement’s Worrisome Embrace of Ibogaine
undark.description: The MAHA movement has been promoting the plant-based substance ibogaine as a remedy for opioid addiction, despite the lack of clinical trials on its safety and efficacy. One physician who practices addiction medicine discusses the risks of ibogaine and argues for the need to support proven treatments.

proj-syn.title: How Developing Countries Can Do More With Less
proj-syn.description: Evaluation frameworks for development projects have long been influenced by donor priorities. But foreign-aid cuts have created an opportunity for African countries to implement equitable evaluation practices, both to channel limited resources more effectively and to shape the future of global development governance.

proj-syn.title: America’s Naval Disaster
proj-syn.description: Plagued by exorbitant costs and chronic delays, American shipbuilders cannot produce enough vessels to keep pace with China. US President Donald Trump’s push to rebuild the industry does little to address its underlying problems and threatens to squander hundreds of billions of dollars.

proj-syn.title: America’s Un-American AI Companies
proj-syn.description: The United States can prevail in the AI race against China by leaning into the strengths of an open society: democratic oversight, the rule of law, robust competition, and open public debate. But that won’t happen as long as American AI companies aggressively lobby against accountability and cozy up to the state.

proj-syn.title: The Golden Bridge to Monetary Multipolarity
proj-syn.description: Gold has overtaken US Treasuries as the world’s top reserve asset because it offers a solution to the challenges of a rogue America. But its renewed relevance also reflects how rapid technological diffusion and increasing dispersion of economic power are creating a more diversified international monetary system.

proj-syn.title: Asia’s Natural Disasters Must Not Become Financial Crises
proj-syn.description: The dangerous flooding in Nepal and Tibet has demonstrated, once again, the need for prearranged disaster-risk financing to prepare for the economic chain reactions triggered by natural disasters. Asia’s policymakers must act now to help cash-strapped Nepal and strengthen other countries’ resilience before the next crisis hits.

proj-syn.title: Is AI Crowding Out Other Investment?
proj-syn.description: The AI investment boom has unleashed a wave of demand for capital just as savings are declining and interest rates remain high. As competition for financing intensifies, rising borrowing costs could squeeze non-AI firms looking to finance new factories, equipment, and projects.

proj-syn.title: India’s Resilience Depends on Diversified Trade
proj-syn.description: India has signed a flurry of trade deals since Donald Trump’s return to the White House in an attempt to ensure that no single bilateral rupture will cause catastrophic harm. It should continue to expand its trade ties, while being wary of any bilateral agreement that curtails its freedom of action vis-à-vis third countries.

proj-syn.title: Whipsaw Trade Policy Is Depressing Foreign Direct Investment
proj-syn.description: If a country opts for higher trade restrictions to promote its perceived domestic interests, a predictable policy is far superior to a volatile one. As new research shows, uncertainty causes unnecessary and large collateral damage to FDI inflows.

proj-syn.title: Why the Far Right’s War on Modern Architecture Matters
proj-syn.description: The Alternative for Germany’s fixation on architecture is more revealing than it may seem. Cultural policy is not only one area where the party can actually change conditions on the ground at the state level; it is also intimately tied to far-right forces’ exclusionary political agenda.

proj-syn.title: How Will the US-Iran War End?
proj-syn.description: The latest US effort to subdue Iran—an "economic D-Day" intended to cut off the Islamic Republic from the world economy—can’t succeed without the support of the country’s biggest trade partner. The only stable solution to the impasse in the Gulf is one that involves China and increases economic integration in the region.

proj-syn.title: Germany’s Political Firewall Is Crumbling
proj-syn.description: The upcoming election in Saxony-Anhalt could give the far-right Alternative für Deutschland control of a state government for the first time in Germany’s postwar history. Its rise offers a crucial lesson for democracies elsewhere: closing ranks against extremist parties is no substitute for effective governance.

proj-syn.title: The Swimmable City Test
proj-syn.description: In committing to provide a safe swimmable place within 15 minutes of every home by 2035, London Mayor Sadiq Khan has set a measurable, time-bound goal that cannot be met through a single program or line item on the budget. Instead, it requires a public mission capable of mobilizing all ministries and shaping markets.

proj-syn.title: The Tale of Economics
proj-syn.description: A new book tells the story of the economics discipline and its original purpose with a degree of verve and imaginativeness that puts dreary mainstream economists to shame. In the process, it gets at fundamental truths that major schools within the discipline have managed to obscure.

proj-syn.title: AI’s Market Path Will Get Bumpier
proj-syn.description: By enhancing the input that goes into so much of what we do—intelligence—AI’s potential to drive higher economic growth is enormous. But with fears of the technology's unintended consequences affecting the pace and depth of adoption, the promise of long-term gains must be set against more immediate risks.

proj-syn.title: American Götterdämmerung
proj-syn.description: US President Donald Trump and his Treasury secretary’s latest desperate threats confirm how much American power has waned on their watch. Far from compelling others to join their efforts to isolate Iran, they are hastening the transition to a post-American world order.

proj-syn.title: Hard Lessons for Europe From the Ceuta Crisis
proj-syn.description: European Union leaders should have received several messages during the recent surge of migrants into the Spanish exclave of Ceuta. In particular, cohesion without trust is fragile; dependence without limits leads to vulnerability; and selective enforcement of international law risks eroding a pillar of Europe’s strategic identity.

proj-syn.title: The World’s Silent Majority for International Cooperation
proj-syn.description: The hollowing out of global institutions has resulted in a rapid loss of credibility for the international rule of law. But a majority of people worldwide still recognize the value of multilateralism, which countries can preserve in the absence of superpower consent by finding better ways to cooperate.

proj-syn.title: Building Canada’s Post-American Economy
proj-syn.description: Canada’s dependence on the US market has become a strategic liability, leaving it vulnerable to President Donald Trump’s bullying. Reducing that dependence will require building industries that can compete globally while removing the structural barriers that prevent innovative Canadian firms from scaling.

With the year’s end now in sight, a small window remains for other startups to launch 2026 IPOs, so we took a look at notable venture-backed startups that Crunchbase’s predictive intelligence suggests are potential IPO candidates within the next six months.

crunchbase.title: Biotech Startup Investment Held Steady Even As AI Funding Surged
crunchbase.description: While the AI boom has disrupted funding patterns across the startup sphere, biotech has remained a rare steady sector for investment. For the past few years, global funding to biotech startups has hovered between $36 billion and $40 billion. Per Crunchbase data, 2026 is on track to stay close to that range.

crunchbase.title: Sector Snapshot: Space Tech Startup Funding Orbits New Highs
